name: Enchanting
migratedFrom: guides218.json professions[2] (2026-11-04), rewritten into a full course on 2026-11-12

overview.lead: Enchanters add stats to gear, and in Forever they can also craft wands, staves and relics.

points.text: Tailoring is the usual partner for cloth casters.
Recipes for the new necklace and two-hand enchants cost Merchant's Favor.

heldBack.text: If enchants still cannot be listed on the Auction House in the live game, income comes from customers you meet in game and from tradeable crafts such as camp features.
heldBack.reason: Whether enchants can be listed is an open question (see 301), and no graded fact says camp features are tradeable.

101.summary: What Enchanting makes in Forever, its camp objects and how to level it.

steps.text: Open the professions window with K, then search or filter the recipe list and track a recipe in the objectives frame.
Look for wand, staff and relic recipes as you level: enchanters can now craft all three.
Place an Enchanted Lute at skill 20, an Arcane Salvager at 140 and an Arcane Forge at 300.
Put the Lute down only when no Druid buff is up: its buff matches Mark of the Wild and does not stack with it.
Sit at the camp for at least 1 minute to get its buff. A basic campsite holds 3 camp features, one per player, so agree in the group who places what.

mistakes.mistake: Placing the Enchanted Lute while a Druid's Mark of the Wild is up.
mistakes.fix: The Lute's buff matches Mark of the Wild and does not stack with it, so it only helps when no Druid buff is up.

mistakes.mistake: Treating Rath'mael in the Ruins of Lordaeron as the settled source of the Arcane Salvager blueprint.
mistakes.fix: Icy Veins puts it there, but another guide disagrees.

steps.text: Train Journeyman at skill 50 and level 10, Expert at skill 125 and level 20, and Artisan at skill 200 and level 35. 300 is the cap.
Build Merchant's Favor by filling Waylaid Crates and handing the sealed crates to Marcy Baker at Three Corners in western Redridge. Craftsman's Writs add reputation.
Necklace enchants need Enchanting 210, Friendly and 120 Merchant's Favor. The two-hand caster enchants need 300, Honored and 240 Favor.
Reaching 150, 225 and 300 for the first time in a craft each earns 1 Legacy point. Dedicated Study gives a daily skill-up, or Elemental Essences once all your skills are 300.
At 300, earn the certification item that unlocks your profession title. Alliance players get it from the Azeroth Commerce Authority.

mistakes.mistake: Waiting at the Journeyman cap of 150 before training Expert.
mistakes.fix: Expert needs skill 125 and level 20, so train it between 125 and 150.

mistakes.mistake: Saving Favor for the two-hand caster enchants before you are Honored.
mistakes.fix: They need Enchanting 300, Honored and 240 Favor. The necklace enchants open earlier, at 210 and Friendly for 120 Favor.

201.summary: The new enchants and caster crafts raiders want, and the market.

chapters.title: Enchants and caster crafts for raiders

steps.text: Learn the new necklace enchants: they add Agility, Deflection, Healing Power, Spell Power or Strength.
For casters and healers on two-hand weapons, offer Mighty Spell Power, Mighty Healing Power or Spellblasting.
Craft the Brilliant Wand for your own use: it is Bind on Pickup for the enchanter.

mistakes.mistake: Promising a raider a Brilliant Wand.
mistakes.fix: It is Bind on Pickup for the enchanter, so only you can use the one you make.

steps.text: The necklace and two-hand enchants are new and cost Merchant's Favor to learn, so they are the services to offer raiders first. Trading is subject to Blizzard policy.
Check the Auction House before you sell surplus crafts to a vendor: Blizzard's beta notes say many profession-made items sell to vendors for less.

mistakes.mistake: Selling surplus crafts to a vendor out of Classic habit.
mistakes.fix: Many profession-made items sell to vendors for less in Forever, so compare the Auction House first.
